DIAGNOSIS READY: Atrial Septal Defect with Congestive Heart Failure.

The test results show a normal BNP and troponin, but the echocardiogram confirms an atrial septal defect causing a left-to-right shunt, which explains your rapid breathing, liver enlargement, and pitting edema due to right-sided heart strain. This rules out multiple sclerosis, which does not present with these specific cardiac and fluid retention symptoms.
